definition: Cookies created and stored by the website you are directly visiting, used to remember your preferences, login status, and provide core website functionality.
metaDescription: Learn about first party cookies - how websites use them to remember your preferences and login status, and why they're essential for web functionality.
simpleExplanation: When you visit a website like Amazon.com, first party cookies are small files that Amazon stores on your browser to remember things like items in your shopping cart or that you're logged in. They only work on that specific website.
whyItMatters: First party cookies enable essential website features like staying logged in, remembering shopping cart contents, and saving preferences. They're generally considered privacy-friendly since they only work on the site that created them.
technicalDetail: First party cookies are set by the domain in your browser's address bar and can only be accessed by that same domain. They're stored locally on your device and sent back to the originating server with each request, enabling stateful interactions on otherwise stateless HTTP connections.

examples.explanation: When you add items to your cart on an e-commerce site, first party cookies remember what you selected even if you navigate to other pages or close your browser temporarily.
After logging into your bank's website, first party cookies keep you authenticated so you don't have to re-enter your credentials on every page.
If you change a website's language from English to Spanish, a first party cookie remembers this choice for future visits to that site.
